name: Accountability: responsible party ensures the conditions are met
framework_text_summary: The responsible party must ensure the conditions for lawful processing, and the measures that give effect to them, are complied with when the purpose and means are decided and during processing.
gap: Organisational measure; the responsible party (the client) attests, with the document or record as evidence. This evidence pack supports accountability for Condition 7 only.
source: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (Government Gazette 37067, 26 Nov 2013), section 8 (Condition 1). https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201409/3706726-11act4of2013protectionofpersonalinforcorrect.pdf (text read from the gazette PDF).
note: POPIA evidence is limited to Condition 7 technical safeguards on systems connected to Liongard. The client must scope which systems hold personal information. The earlier POPIA dashboard did this with a "Compliance Basis" widget, and Ops Portal needs the same declaration. The MSP is usually an operator (s20-21) for the client, so the s21 contract and s21(2) notification duty apply to the MSP itself.

name: Measures to prevent loss of, damage to or unauthorised destruction of personal information
framework_text_summary: Secure integrity and confidentiality with appropriate, reasonable technical and organisational measures to prevent loss, damage or unauthorised destruction.
tested: Backup inspectors (by stack capability or product name) that are fresh, plus current job findings that read failed, missed or stale. Does not test per-job recency, offsite copies or restore tests. Managed endpoints (Windows agent, RMM or EDR seen) with an EDR product reported, or Microsoft Defender antivirus and real-time protection on. Fails on any endpoint where protection is off or absent.
gap: Technical measures on the systems Liongard sees. Restore testing, offsite or immutable copies and physical protection are not evidenced; organisational measures are attested. Liongard sees systems, not personal information: it cannot tell which systems hold personal information. The client scopes that (the earlier POPIA dashboard's "Compliance Basis" widget).
source: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (Government Gazette 37067, 26 Nov 2013), section 19(1)(a) (Condition 7). https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201409/3706726-11act4of2013protectionofpersonalinforcorrect.pdf (text read from the gazette PDF).

name: Measures to prevent unlawful access to or processing of personal information
framework_text_summary: Appropriate, reasonable technical and organisational measures to prevent unlawful access to or processing of personal information.
tested: Enabled accounts with admin rights in any inspected identity system, and whether each has MFA reported in every system it exists in (Identity & access "Admins without MFA"). MFA here is registration as reported by the source (for Microsoft 365, isMFARegistered, which needs Entra ID P1 and stays "Enabled" after MFA is switched off). Share of enabled people and admin accounts with MFA reported in every system they exist in. Pass at 98% or more, partial at 80% or more. Registration, not enforcement. Accounts disabled in at least one system but still present or holding admin rights in another inspected tool (excluding AD, Microsoft 365, KnowBe4, dark web). Enabled accounts with no sign-in for 90+ days or reported stale by a source; accounts with no sign-in data are named, not passed. Enabled personal accounts that hold a top-level admin role (global admin, super admin, owner, domain admin) instead of a separate admin account. Open BitLocker or "not encrypted" alerts on Windows devices, plus any current encryption-off finding from other tools. A device with no alert counts as encrypted.
gap: Access controls on inspected identity systems and endpoints. Application-level permissions on the systems that hold personal information, and data-level access, are not seen. MFA is registration; encryption is alert-based. Liongard sees systems, not personal information: it cannot tell which systems hold personal information. The client scopes that (the earlier POPIA dashboard's "Compliance Basis" widget).
source: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (Government Gazette 37067, 26 Nov 2013), section 19(1)(b) (Condition 7). https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201409/3706726-11act4of2013protectionofpersonalinforcorrect.pdf (text read from the gazette PDF).

name: Identify all reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks
framework_text_summary: Take reasonable measures to identify all reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks to personal information in the responsible party's possession or control.
tested: Technical risks Liongard finds on inspected systems: unsupported operating systems, missing updates, unmanaged devices on the network and spoofable email domains. Every endpoint seen (managed and unmanaged) whose operating system is past its vendor end-of-support date. Agent-reporting Windows endpoints with any update waiting in Windows Update (AvailableUpdates). No severity, no age, no third-party applications, no firmware. Endpoints seen by discovery tools that have no RMM, EDR or Liongard agent. Inspected domains that are spoofable (no enforcing DMARC or failing SPF for sending domains; no reject policy and -all SPF for non-sending domains).
gap: Technical risks only, on systems connected to Liongard. People, process, supplier and physical risks, and the risk assessment itself, are the client's (the page's "risk assessment" policy question). Liongard sees systems, not personal information: it cannot tell which systems hold personal information. The client scopes that (the earlier POPIA dashboard's "Compliance Basis" widget).
source: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (Government Gazette 37067, 26 Nov 2013), section 19(2)(a) (Condition 7). https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201409/3706726-11act4of2013protectionofpersonalinforcorrect.pdf (text read from the gazette PDF).

name: Establish and maintain appropriate safeguards against the risks identified
framework_text_summary: Establish and maintain appropriate safeguards against the identified risks.
tested: Whether core technical safeguards are in place and maintained on inspected systems. Managed endpoints (Windows agent, RMM or EDR seen) with an EDR product reported, or Microsoft Defender antivirus and real-time protection on. Fails on any endpoint where protection is off or absent. Windows Firewall on for the domain, private and public profiles on agent-reporting Windows endpoints. Open BitLocker or "not encrypted" alerts on Windows devices, plus any current encryption-off finding from other tools. A device with no alert counts as encrypted. Enabled accounts with admin rights in any inspected identity system, and whether each has MFA reported in every system it exists in (Identity & access "Admins without MFA"). MFA here is registration as reported by the source (for Microsoft 365, isMFARegistered, which needs Entra ID P1 and stays "Enabled" after MFA is switched off). Backup inspectors (by stack capability or product name) that are fresh, plus current job findings that read failed, missed or stale. Does not test per-job recency, offsite copies or restore tests. Agent-reporting Windows endpoints with any update waiting in Windows Update (AvailableUpdates). No severity, no age, no third-party applications, no firmware.
gap: Shows technical safeguards exist and are maintained; does not show they are "appropriate" to the client's risks (that is a judgement tied to 19(2)(a) and 19(3)). Organisational safeguards (policies, contracts, training content) are attested. Liongard sees systems, not personal information: it cannot tell which systems hold personal information. The client scopes that (the earlier POPIA dashboard's "Compliance Basis" widget).
source: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (Government Gazette 37067, 26 Nov 2013), section 19(2)(b) (Condition 7). https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201409/3706726-11act4of2013protectionofpersonalinforcorrect.pdf (text read from the gazette PDF).

name: Regularly verify that safeguards are effectively implemented
framework_text_summary: Take reasonable measures to regularly verify that the safeguards are effectively implemented.
tested: That Liongard re-inspects the systems on a schedule and its data is current, so the technical safeguards above are being verified regularly. Each saved snapshot (compliance-history.json) is a dated verification. Share of active Liongard inspectors whose data is current against their own schedule. This is the quality of Liongard's own evidence, not a client control.
gap: Automated verification of technical configuration only. Verification of organisational safeguards, and independent testing (penetration tests, audits), are attested. This is the one place the "evidence" check is a genuine control mapping.
source: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (Government Gazette 37067, 26 Nov 2013), section 19(2)(c) (Condition 7). https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201409/3706726-11act4of2013protectionofpersonalinforcorrect.pdf (text read from the gazette PDF).

name: Continually update safeguards in response to new risks or deficiencies
framework_text_summary: Ensure safeguards are continually updated in response to new risks or deficiencies in earlier safeguards.
tested: Supporting only: the remediation list (marked done, verified fixed, reopened) and the trend between snapshots show deficiencies being closed.
gap: Updating safeguards is a management process; the remediation record supports the attestation but is not itself a safeguard check.
source: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (Government Gazette 37067, 26 Nov 2013), section 19(2)(d) (Condition 7). https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201409/3706726-11act4of2013protectionofpersonalinforcorrect.pdf (text read from the gazette PDF).

name: Due regard to generally accepted information security practices

gap: The client names the practice it follows (for example CIS Controls v8.1 or ISO/IEC 27001). That framework's catalogue in this folder then shows what Liongard evidences against it. The Information Regulator's Dis-Chem enforcement notice relied on s19 (secondary source: https://inforegulator.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/DIS-CHEM-ENFORCEMENT-NOTICE.pdf, not read in full).
